A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Jailbreak Antidote and retain matching methods and experiments. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original defense-success and utility evaluations across nine LLMs, along with representation analyses and sparsity/scaling-factor ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds safety-alignment comparisons, adaptive-attack evaluations, downstream utility results, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions derive a safety direction through PCA, select its largest-magnitude components, and add the scaled masked direction to hidden states during inference. v3 explains the eigendecomposition explicitly but introduces no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU and HellaSwag evaluations for factual knowledge and commonsense reasoning (Table A.8). It also adds defense-targeted adaptive GCG, PAIR, and AutoDAN scenarios (Table A.4), substantially extending the original static-attack and AlpacaEval coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 2 evaluates safety-alignment comparators Llama-3-8B-it-RR (Zou et al., 2024) and Gemma-2-9B-it-DSA (Qi et al., 2024a), including combinations with Antidote. The original six defenses remain. Adding evaluated alignment defenses substantially broadens the comparison beyond the original inference-time defenses.

E3.justification: v3 adds adaptive attacks against fixed Antidote parameters, including Llama-2-7B/13B-chat configurations, length-controlled AlpacaEval scoring, and direct runtime/precomputation measurements. Table 2 specifies that aligned-model utility is compared against the corresponding original models. The original static evaluation and alpha ranges remain.

E4.justification: The existing alpha, sparsity, and random-selection ablations remain. v3 adds dataset-similarity checks (Table A.1), adaptive-attack robustness tests (Table A.4), response-length controls (Table A.5), and benign-refusal analysis (Figure A.9). Token-position analyses also expand to multiple explicitly identified models.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental results. The retained component-distribution plots do not represent experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1's original scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds extensive results under new conditions. Table A.4 reports baseline/Antidote GCG DSR of 46/83% for Llama-2-7B-chat; Table A.8 reports Antidote scores of 67.4 on MMLU and 82.5 on HellaSwag for Llama-3-8B-it. Alignment, length-controlled utility, timing, similarity, and refusal results are also newly reported. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v3 Equations 4–5 spell out the eigendecomposition and leading eigenvector already implicit in v1's first-principal-component construction. This restates existing mathematics; neither version supplies additional theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of sparse runtime safety adjustment, approximately 5% activation modification, and balancing safety with utility remain. The negative-alpha warning highlighted in v3's conclusion was already documented in v1 Section 5.3 and Appendix A.2.5.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of compatibility with safety-aligned models and explains shorter inference times through shorter safe responses. It explicitly identifies adversaries exploiting internal-state adjustments as an unresolved limitation. These qualify and extend the discussion while retaining the original sparsity mechanism and safety–utility interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 discloses NVIDIA A100 80GB hardware, one-/two-GPU configurations, the Transformers framework, and precomputation costs in Appendix A.2.10. It also supplies a specific attack-artifact source link. Existing alpha ranges, sampling of 20 alpha values, and judge instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds brief coverage of SafeDecoding and citations to activation engineering and pruning/low-rank safety research. References also expand for the new alignment comparisons and benchmarks. The basic positioning around sparse inference-time control remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and main section sequence remain largely intact. Changes include localized related-work and conclusion rewrites, expanded PCA explanation, revised efficiency discussion, new appendix subsections, and updated affiliations/contact information.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displays with new comparison and analysis tables, runtime and refusal plots, and additional token-position heatmaps. v1 Figure 4 moves to Figure A.10, while v3 Figure 4 uses runtime on its horizontal axis. The retained response-example table moves from A.3 to A.9 and loses its red/blue output coding despite retaining the color-based caption.

improvement.justification: v1 supported robustness mainly with static attack prompts and efficiency with token counts. v3 adds defense-targeted adaptive tests (Table A.4), measured runtime and preparation costs (Figure 4; Tables A.6–A.7), alignment comparisons, and downstream utility checks, substantially strengthening evidence for the central claims. Adaptive-attack budgets remain underspecified, and the claim of consistently superior length-controlled win rates overlooks Gemma-2-9B-it in Table A.5. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial validation gains.
